claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has severe lattice distortion because of its multielement composition.
The lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr alters dislocation core structures.
Altered dislocation cores in WTaTiVZr produce wavy dislocation lines.
Wavy dislocation lines promote distributed plastic deformation and delay crack initiation.
As-cast and homogenized equimolar WTaTiVZr is primarily a single-phase refractory BCC material.
The homogenized WTaTiVZr initial state has high lattice distortion.
Temperatures of 700–900°C are representative of plasma-facing-component service.
Wavy dislocation lines in WTaTiVZr obstruct dislocation channeling and reduce local stress concentrations.
Differences among the atomic radii of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr generate severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion causes dislocation cores to deviate from their neutral glide planes.
The resulting wavy dislocation geometry makes plastic flow more homogeneous than in pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr will have greater strain to failure than commercially used pure tungsten during high-temperature testing.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr will absorb more energy before fracture and therefore exhibit enhanced toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten exhibits limited plasticity and comparatively brittle failure under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Pure tungsten has well-documented lower ductility and more brittle behavior under similar high-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies primarily when temperature is high enough to thermally activate dislocation motion.
Abnormal grain-boundary decohesion, very low temperature, or extreme irradiation can invalidate the proposed deformation mechanism.
Minor precipitates or grain-boundary effects could modulate the mechanical behavior of WTaTiVZr independently of lattice distortion.
